hook: SCP-1972 pairs two anomalies the Foundation is careful to keep apart: an antlered, tentacled humanoid who worked as a prostitute in Montreal and a flying metal sphere that wants her dead. The article is short and the punchline sits in the very last line, so read it straight through. It deals frankly with sex work, including clients solicited in groups.
whyItMatters: It is a compact setup that works like a joke with a long fuse, with the description, the recovery log and two interviews each adding one piece. The contrast in voices does most of the work: one subject talks warmly and casually about her trade, the other speaks in all-caps legal pronouncements. It shows how much character an entry can build out of interviews alone.
thingsToNotice:
Small details in the procedures pay off later: contact limited to female staff, a vocal modulator against compulsion effects, a sterilisation plan covering three sets of ovaries, and a marsupial-like pouch on her abdomen. SCP-1972-A presents her work as kindness, offering lonely, struggling people a little love and nudging a few toward a better life, while most people who meet her in person accept how she looks.

SCP-1972-B, speaking with Dr. Taylor in her role as its assigned defence lawyer, lists charges from grand prostitution to dealing in unprocessed orgone, and saves the gravest for last: seducing an officer of justice. Its final line reveals that it is that officer and that it is pregnant, which recasts the 43 dead staff and the plasma-firing chase as a matter of personal honour.
